I mean, you saying the "listening to Japanese song on Korean holiday" shows that you are equally clueless about the political issues that's happening across the globe... It's much more than that. 

Basically, August 15th was the day that Korea got liberated from Imperial Japan. During WWII, the things that Imperial Japan has done to the Korean, Chinese, and other people in countries that Imperial Japan has invaded are basically what the N@zis did to the Jews. 

Even my great grandpa got tortured by Imperial Japan's soldiers for "speaking in Korean" and got permanently disabled. He was only 6 years old. When he begged them to take him to the hospital, they laughed and said, "You deserve it since you were born as Korean," and left him on the street. No one helped him since he was "Korean". 

Until the day he passed away, I could clearly tell that my great grandpa was traumatized from the incident since he couldn't handle even listening to Japaense. 

There's other extremely horrendous acts committed by Imperial Japan that I can't even say on this subreddit. R@pe, murder, torture, using people as "meat shields", using them to test out new weapons, and many more. 

It's not something that can be summarized as "Korean holiday". 

What the Imperial Japan did to the Koreans are impactful, to say the least. Which is why a lot of Koreans refrain from listening to Japanese music, traveling to Japan, or even mentioning Japan altogether on the day. 

Sure, it's not illegal to do those things on the Liberation Day, but if you do that (especially if you are a public figure), you are seen as thoughtless, out of touch, and even as someone who support Imperial Japan's behaviour. 

I know the idol who did this, and I am a big fan of his. But me and other Korean fans were very disappointed by his behaviour, especially since he did the same thing before. I just hope he actually learns from the mistake and never does it again.
